description: External, versioned access policy for the knowledge-graph PoC and the authorization trust boundary's source of truth. Kept OUTSIDE the graph and versioned separately from both the data and the ontology. Authorization is two-dimensional: role-based capability grants (which sensitivity CATEGORIES of fields, which ENTITIES, and whether aggregates are allowed) plus CLEARANCE (gated against each node's in-graph `classification` for row-level visibility). The `catalog` is the curated, queryable surface the structured-intent query builder validates typed queries against; a field absent from the catalog is queryable by no one (default-deny).

Aircraft.description: The aircraft (airframe) the knowledge graph describes.

Specification.description: Published performance specifications and limits for the aircraft type.

Aerodrome.description: An aerodrome (airport) that appears in the network the aircraft operates in.

System.description: A major aircraft system (e.g. airframe, electrical, powerplant).

Component.description: A maintainable component or part fitted to the aircraft.

Document.description: A maintenance or reference document (manual, AD, service bulletin).

Flight.description: A flight flown by the aircraft. Duration fields are maintenance-relevant; route fields (departure/destination/distance/altitude) are restricted; whole classified (e.g. military) flights are gated by clearance.

identities.description: Default identity for unknown or unselected users. Least privilege: basic reference data about the aircraft, its published specifications, and aerodromes. No maintenance history, no flight durations, no flight routes, no aggregates. Unrecognised user ids resolve to this identity (default-deny).

Maintains the airframe, engine and components. Cleared to see flight durations and maintenance history (components, documents, performance), and to run aggregates, but NOT flight routes (departure/destination/distance) and NOT classified flights.

Operations role cleared to the highest level. May see everything maintenance can, PLUS flight routes, aerodrome coordinates, and classified (e.g. military) flights that other identities cannot see at all.
